packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (isolated first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier
reading of these leaves. I have not tried to identify work or author. Biblical or patristic
source names appear below only where the scribe writes a citation siglum himself.

====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
====================================================================
Observations
- Three overviews (image-001, -004, -007/-010) show an album or guard-book page of tan paper
  onto which several parchment pieces are mounted. Text is upright in all tiles.
- Piece A (image-001; tiles 002, 003): a roughly square parchment leaf, one column, long
  lines, about 25 lines, complete at left and right, modern ink foliation "86" top right, a
  small ink mark "11"(?) at the top centre edge. A red circular library stamp at the left
  margin, partly legible "...E IMPERIALE ... MAN." Small cursive-influenced book hand, brown
  ink, heavily abbreviated. Red paraph marks; some initials touched in red. No running title.
- Piece B (image-004; tiles 005, 006): the other side of a leaf of the same size and hand (a
  mirror-reversed "86" shows through at top left), one column, about 25 lines. A two-line red
  initial M at tile 006 line 3-4, with a marginal guide letter "m" and a mark beside it. A
  small marginal cross sign to the left of image-005 line 11. At the right of the same
  opening, across a gutter/guard, begins the leaf foliated "87".
- Piece C recto (image-007; tiles 008, 009): leaf "87", a narrower piece; the line ENDS are
  cut away at the right (trimmed leaf). About 26 lines. Underlined words in black at tile 009
  lines 5 and 7; red paraphs; a black ink blot at 008 line 12; small holes.
- Piece C verso (image-010; tiles 011, 012): the other side of "87" (reversed "87" shows
  through top left); here the line BEGINNINGS are lost at the left. About 25 lines.
  Underlined ordinal words (see below), red-touched initials, one red paraph.
- Above these pieces in every overview are two further narrow parchment strips in a
  different, smaller and more angular hand, each showing only the first few letters of some
  20-25 lines. They are present only at overview scale; no native tile was supplied.
Tentative interpretation (not established)
- A-B-C look like consecutive leaves of one small-format prose text of a preaching or
  devotional kind: a series organised by the hours of the day with a repeated refrain, then a
  new section opened by the red M with a scriptural lemma, then enumerated lists ("triplex",
  "septem"), with short citation sigla (Jo., Job, G., Au., ps., ecc.). I did not observe
  glosses or a separate commentary layer; citations run inside the main text.

Areas selected: every line of the four native-resolution text faces (A, B left page, C recto,
C verso). Unread: the two upper strips (overview only - a native crop is needed), and the
lost line ends of C recto / line beginnings of C verso.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion of an abbreviation; ? after a word = uncertain reading;
[...] = text lost by trimming or damage; [illegible] = present but not read. Line numbers
count from the top of each image file. ¶ = red paraph.
